title: Long-horizon sequence emulator and spectral tail mapper
text:
Long-horizon sequence emulator and spectral tail mapper

body:
Motivation: We frequently observe latent degradation in per-token latency and memory usage when serving requests that span several thousand tokens (long-horizon dialogs or document completions). Existing benchmarks cover steady-state short- and mid-length sequences but do not reproduce interaction patterns that cause kernel backpressure, KV cache churn, or tail amplification. This PR introduces a new long-horizon sequence emulator (LHSE) and an accompanying spectral tail mapper reporter to expose frequency-domain signatures of tail events across kernels and micro-batching slots. The change is intended for the benchmark lab: a representative workload runner that exercises realistic tokenizer splits, interleaved priming and streaming steps, and session-level warmup behavior; plus a reporting pipeline that correlates latency quantiles with kernel-level sampling spectra so SRE and runtime teams can triage long-tail regressions. Changes: added runner binary and harness, new protobuf for long-horizon workload definitions, a lightweight sampler that can capture per-step telemetry, a spectral mapper module that consumes telemetry and produces per-kernel spectrograms and tail attribution summaries, e2e benchmark and unit tests, and CI matrix entries. Notable constraints: runner has a configurable memory ceiling and synthetic priming modes; the spectral mapper is offline-only (we convert to streaming in a follow-up). Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing short/mid-length benchmarks or CI presets. How to use: ./bin/lhse --config examples/long_horizon/demo.yaml to run locally; report generation: ./tools/spectral-mapper --input traces/*.ndjson --out reports/spectral-<ts>.json. Benchmarks and sample reports included in /benchmarks/long_horizon/samples. Summary of results: on a 48GB A100 instance with sequence horizon 4096 and microbatch 8 the runner produces a p95 of 74ms and a p99 of 210ms in our simulated mixed-dialog workload; spectral mapper highlights recurring kernel hotbands at attention and kvcache eviction windows. Related work: ENG-4123 (long-tail regression story), ENG-4970 (kvcache lifecycle tuning).

performance_summary:
Representative run (A100-48GB, microbatch=8, horizon=4096): p50=22ms, p90=58ms, p95=74ms, p99=210ms. Spectral mapper indicates periodic spikes aligned with attention recompute windows and KV cache eviction; recommends exploring staggered KV checkpointing and slot-aware prefetching.

review_comments:
Diego Marquez: Nice approach; can you add a flag to throttle token emit rate to simulate slower clients?
Author (Aisha Khan): Added --token-rate flag in second commit; default preserves prior behavior.
Priya Patel: spectral-mapper dependency on scipy might be heavy for CI — consider optional install or wheel caching.
Author (Aisha Khan): moved scipy import to optional extras and added minimal fallback (FFT from numpy) for CI runs.
Jonah Li: tests look good; I want an example of a failing trace to exercise the mapper end-to-end.
Author (Aisha Khan): included a synthetic failure trace in samples and a short note in the README.

release_notes:
Adds long-horizon sequence emulator and offline spectral tail mapper for long-tail analysis. Provides new benchmark runner and reporting pipeline under benchmarks/long_horizon. No API or runtime-breaking changes. Suggested follow-ups: streaming mapper and KV prefetch probe (ENG-5241).
